fullPassage: The Stoics were a philosophical school that flourished in the Greco-Roman world from the fourth century BC to the second century AD. Originating with Zeno of Citium in Cyprus (335-265 BC) but eventually spreading to Athens, Rome, and the rest of the Roman Empire, Stoicism had a major influence on ancient civilization. Although they are best known for their ethical views, the Stoics also had views on logic, epistemology, metaphysics, and natural science. The Stoics believed living things were composed of passive matter and an active force they called pneuma. They identified God as the intelligent designer of the world who keeps it evolving and changing according to strict natural laws. The most important question for the Stoics was how a person should live. Their answer was: One should seek happiness - in Greek, eudaimonia. But what is happiness? For the Stoics, happiness was an "excellent activity of the soul" - being virtuous, courageous, modest, and patient. They believed it was reasonable to desire things like wealth, fame, and health, but happiness had nothing to do with actually possessing them. Indeed, the Stoics believed that a person who was fully virtuous could be happy regardless of his or her physical well-being. The person could be happy even while being tortured. Further, the Stoics believed that emotions are not merely feelings but always involve beliefs. For instance, they thought being afraid of disease required believing that disease was bad. However, since a truly virtuous person could be happy in the face of disease, it was wrong to believe that disease is bad. Therefore, the Stoics recommended purging emotion.

questions.stem:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

The Stoics were a philosophical school that flourished in the Greco-Roman world from the fourth century BC to the second century AD. Although they are best known for their ethical views, the Stoics also had views on logic, epistemology, metaphysics, and natural science.

(A) For the Stoics, happiness was an "excellent activity of the soul" - being virtuous, courageous, modest, and patient. They believed it was reasonable to desire things like wealth, fame, and health, but happiness had nothing to do with actually possessing them.

(B) The most important question for the Stoics was how a person should live. Their answer was: One should seek happiness - in Greek, eudaimonia. But what is happiness?

(C) Indeed, the Stoics believed that a person who was fully virtuous could be happy regardless of his or her physical well-being. The person could be happy even while being tortured. Further, the Stoics believed that emotions are not merely feelings but always involve beliefs.

det.korean: 스토아 학파는 윤리관으로 가장 잘 알려져 있지만 논리학 등에 대한 견해도 있었다. (B) 가장 중요한 질문은 '어떻게 살아야 하는가'였고 답은 행복 추구였다. 그러나 행복이 무엇인지 물었다. (A) 행복은 영혼의 훌륭한 활동이며 덕, 용기 등이고, 부·명예·건강의 소유와는 무관하다. (C) 실제로 완전히 덕이 있는 사람은 신체 상태와 무관하게 행복할 수 있으며, 감정은 믿음을 포함한다.
det.analysis:
① (A) - (C) - (B)
→ 행복의 정의(A)가 질문 제기(B)보다 먼저 나와 논리적 흐름이 끊긴다.

② (B) - (C) - (A)
→ 질문 제기(B) 후 바로 미덕/감정 논의(C)로 건너뛰어 행복의 정의(A)가 누락된 순서가 된다.

③ (C) - (B) - (A)
→ 미덕 논의(C)가 가장 먼저 나와 이유 없이 결론부터 제시되는 부자연스러운 순서다.

④ (B) - (A) - (C) ← 정답
→ (B)에서 '어떻게 살아야 하는가'라는 질문과 행복(eudaimonia) 추구를 제시하고, (A)에서 행복이 무엇인지 구체적으로 설명하며, (C)에서 미덕과 감정에 대한 추가 논의로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.
det.tip: 지시어(this, their 등)와 연결어(But, Indeed, Further)를 통해 문단 간 논리적 연결을 파악하라.

→ 두려움의 예시 설명 중간에 재진술 문장이 끼어들면 예시의 흐름이 끊긴다.

④ the political influence of Stoicism on the Roman Empire
→ 로마 제국에 대한 정치적 영향력은 본문에서 다루지 않는다.

questions.passage: The Stoics were a philosophical school that flourished in the Greco-Roman world from the fourth century BC to the second century AD. Originating with Zeno of Citium in Cyprus (335-265 BC) but eventually spreading to Athens, Rome, and the rest of the Roman Empire, Stoicism had a major influence on ancient civilization. Although they are best known for their ethical views, the Stoics also had views on logic, epistemology, metaphysics, and natural science. The Stoics believed living things were composed of passive matter and an active force they called pneuma. They identified God as the intelligent designer of the world who keeps it evolving and changing according to strict natural laws. The most important question for the Stoics was how a person should live. Their answer was: One should seek happiness - in Greek, eudaimonia. But what is happiness? For the Stoics, happiness was an "excellent activity of the soul" - being virtuous, courageous, modest, and patient. They believed it was reasonable to desire things like wealth, fame, and health, but happiness had nothing to do with actually possessing them. Indeed, the Stoics believed that a person who was fully virtuous could be happy regardless of his or her physical well-being. The person could be happy even while being tortured. Further, the Stoics believed that emotions are not merely feelings but always involve beliefs. For instance, they thought being afraid of disease required believing that disease was bad. However, since a truly virtuous person could be happy in the face of disease, it was wrong to believe that disease is bad. Therefore, the Stoics recommended purging emotion.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 (compose)를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 스토아 학파는 생물이 소극적인 물질과 그들이 프네우마라고 부르는 능동적인 힘으로 구성되어 있다고 믿었다.
det.analysis: 정답 ✅: 주어 living things가 '구성되는' 대상이므로 수동형이 필요하며, 문맥상 과거시제이므로 compose를 과거분사 composed로 바꾸어 were composed(수동태)를 완성해야 한다.
det.tip: 주어가 행위의 대상이면 수동태(be+p.p.)를 사용한다.

questions.passage: They believed it was reasonable to desire things like wealth, fame, and health, but happiness had nothing to do with actually possessing them. Indeed, the Stoics believed that a person who was fully __________ could be happy regardless of his or her physical well-being. The person could be happy even while being tortured.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 (virtue)를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 실제로 스토아 학파는 완전히 덕이 있는 사람은 신체적 안녕과 무관하게 행복할 수 있다고 믿었다.
det.analysis: 정답 ✅: be동사 was 뒤에서 사람의 상태를 설명하는 형용사가 필요하므로 명사 virtue를 형용사형 virtuous로 바꾸어야 한다.
det.tip: be동사의 보어 자리에는 형용사가 와야 한다.
